quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead of you. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. You must be careful when passing them. On a hill with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When you see this sign, it means:

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. There may be several of these signs along the curve.

questions.question: You must use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: They are deaf.
They are a police officer.
They are blind.
They have poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger directs you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to. Not all crossings have gates or lights. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: When approaching an accident, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived yet.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Keep your attention on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Never stop just to look at an accident, fire, or disaster.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the road shoulder with no one inside.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
If you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop while the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: You are in an accident and someone is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless necessary. Moving them incorrectly can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is severe bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
Safely change lanes and back up to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the proper lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need more effort to steer. Slow down and carefully drive to a safe area to stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangle sign means yield. Slow down at the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign tells you to slow down and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if necessary.

questions.question: A driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Give the vehicle extra space.
Know that the driver is distracted and less safe.
Do not copy that driver's behavior.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to crash.

questions.question: Distracted drivers crash more often when they use which of these?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving takes your attention away from the road and increases your crash risk.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive normally like nothing is wrong.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Take time to calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take time to calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness can distract you from driving. Calm down and get focused before you start driving.

questions.question: You notice a problem with your vehicle that may affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have enough money.
Drive slower.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any vehicle problem that affects safe driving right away before you drive.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move ahead or drop back so the driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move ahead or drop back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or backward so they can see you.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers which way you plan to turn.

questions.question: Stopping completely, letting other traffic and pedestrians go first, then going through the intersection matches which light?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means what color light will come next?

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive next to them and do not follow too close behind them.
Flash your lights at them.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not follow too close behind them.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and back. Do not drive alongside them or tailgate them.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a car crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the most effective way to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Protecting yourself against poor drivers by passing them in traffic.
Following the car ahead of you closely.
Quickly changing lanes and moving through traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. This helps you avoid problems with reckless, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: Another driver is trying to pass your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.
Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing vehicle can move back into the right lane safely and easily.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When must a vehicle buyer transfer ownership and registration?

options.text: By the end of the year.
Before the license plate expires.
Within 15 days from the date of purchase.
Within 60 days from the date of purchase.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 15 days from the date of purchase.
questions.explanation: A vehicle buyer must transfer ownership within 15 days to avoid penalty fees. If a dealer sells the vehicle, the dealer is responsible for the transfer.
